message.content: If the ratio is \(R_{\text{gt}} / R_{\text{own}}\), a larger value only means \(R_{\text{gt}}\) is high relative to \(R_{\text{own}}\). If your target is to minimize the model’s own-prefix repetition \(R_{\text{own}}\), then—holding \(R_{\text{gt}}\) fixed—a larger ratio is better because it indicates a smaller denominator. If your target is to minimize the ground-truth-prefix repetition \(R_{\text{gt}}\), or to minimize both absolute repetition rates, a larger ratio is not inherently better; it may just reflect a larger numerator. So the safest answer is: lower absolute repetition is better; the ratio by itself is ambiguous. ((([[{{{larger ratio is not intrinsically better or worse}}}]])
